predecessors.note: The Pushyabhuti page's infobox lists the Maukharis among its predecessor/successor entries without saying which. The Maukhari page says 'the Maukhari territories where eventually absorbed into the territory of Harsha' and 'After the demise of the Maukharis, it even became the capital of Emperor Harsha'; the Kannauj page says Harsha 'made it his capital' (r. 606 to 647); none gives a year. This dossier takes only the Kannauj circle in 606 (/ledger/1); the rest of the Maukhari plain is drawn from the 612 gain. The maukhari-dynasty dissolve of 606 hands Harsha the whole realm, which the pages do not support for 606 (see notes).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the row in 612, six years after the April 606 coronation. The core is Haryana around Thanesar plus the Kannauj circle that /ledger/1 gains in 606 (the ledger and this keyframe agree; repair of the review finding). The Harsha page dates the early conquests to 606-612 (Mookerji and Vaidya), so the growth from this core to the 612 shape is the 612 gain event (confidence 2). The rest of the Maukhari realm (Uttar Pradesh east of Kannauj, Bihar outside Magadha, Nepal) is undated on the Maukhari page ('eventually absorbed') and is drawn from 612, not before.

Gauda page: 'Gauda was soon divided amongst Harshavardhana and Bhaskarvarmana of Kamarupa'; the page does not say which share was Harsha's, so Cliopatria's Bengal cells are kept as the reading, minus the 294 cells of the Khadga outline (the Khadga page rules 'Vanga and Samatata' from 625; the Cliopatria Harsha shape wrongly includes 292 of them) and the 28-cell Karnasuvarna circle that kamarupa-kingdom gains in 637. Cliopatria's 0.965 M km2 for 644-646 against the infobox's 1,000,000 km2 (estimate for 648): ratio 0.97; after the corrections 3257 cells (about 0.82 M km2, ratio 0.82; with the Magadha vassal about 0.86 M km2), still within a factor of two. Verdict changed from ok to adjust: the shape included the Khadga cells and Magadha. 'his empire covered much of north and north-western India, extending till Kamarupa in the east and Narmada River in the south' agrees; the page gives no finer boundary.

Harsha 'died without an heir, leading to the end of the Pushyabhuti dynasty' in 647; the only successor named is Arunasva 'as King of Kannauj', so the empire's own shape ends in 647 and this is the successor's seat, not Harsha's land

keyframe_review.note: The 647-655 shape (161,252 km2, West Bengal and Bangladesh) is not Harsha's: Bengal was Gauda's land divided in 636/637 and the dynasty ended with Harsha in 647. Do not draw this shape in Harsha's colour; the ledger's dissolve event ends the state in 647 and the land goes to the successors (Arunasva at Kannauj; Vanga and Samatata to the Khadga dynasty, which the Khadga page dates from 625).

ledger.note: 606: Harsha is crowned at Thanesar. 'Subsequently, in 606 CE, Harsha was formally crowned as an emperor' (Pushyabhuti page); Harsha page: 'crowned him emperor at an assembly in April 606'. The pages give the seat, not a boundary.

606: Kanyakubja (Kannauj) joins the Thanesar realm. The Harsha, Maukhari and Kannauj pages are silent on the year: the Harsha page says he 'eventually' made Kanyakubja his capital, the Maukhari page that its territories 'eventually' passed to Harsha, and the Kannauj page that it was the greatest city 'under Emperor Harsha (r. 606 to 647 CE) who made it his capital'. 606 is the year taken from the maukhari-dynasty dossier, which ends the Maukharis then; month 4 is only the coronation month, the earliest the gain can fall (repair: the event no longer sorts before the founding).

606: Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa offers his alliance. Pushyabhuti page: 'Overlordship was accepted by the king of Vallabhi (west) and Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa (east)', undated; the Kamarupa page ties his alliance to Harsha's accession in 606 but does not call him Harsha's subordinate, so the page disagreement is noted and the tint is the researcher's choice. Month 4 is the coronation month (placeholder, so the event sorts after the founding).

region.text: Kamarupa under Bhaskaravarman ('Bhaskarvarman (600-650)'), allied with Harsha against Shashanka

ledger.note: 606: the Later Guptas of Magadha rule as Harsha's vassals. Later Gupta page: 'the Pushyabhuti emperor Harsa (ruled c. 606 - c. 647 CE) restored the Later Gupta rule in Magadha and they ruled as Harsa's vassals'. The page gives no year for the restoration; 606 is the start of Harsha's reign and the year the later-gupta-dynasty dossier uses (its /ledger/8), so the year is a bridge (confidence 1). Magadha is drawn by later-gupta-dynasty and is taken out of this state's direct shapes (repair of the review finding: Magadha was drawn twice).

region.text: Magadha, 'the Magadha region of what is now Bihar', where Harsha 'restored the Later Gupta rule'

ledger.note: 612: the early conquests are complete. The Harsha page says Mookerji and Vaidya date the early conquests to 606-612, and the Pushyabhuti page says Xuanzang had him march from west to east subduing insubordinate kings early in his reign (paraphrases); those kings are not a polity, so the counterpart is 'nobody' (repair of the review finding). Cliopatria's first shape is 612. The region includes the Maukhari plain beyond the Kannauj circle: the maukhari-dynasty dissolve of 606 hands that land to Harsha at once, while the Maukhari page says only that it was 'eventually absorbed' (no year), so here it enters by 612 at the latest. Bengal is left out because it was Shashanka's, Magadha because it is the Later Gupta vassal, the strip south of the Narmada because no page gives it to Harsha.

region.text: much of north and north-western India as Cliopatria draws it for 612, without Shashanka's Bengal, without Magadha, without the strip south of the Narmada, and without the Haryana and Kannauj core held since 606

ledger.note: Nov 618: Harsha marches to the Narmada. 'the conflict took place between November 618 CE and February 619 CE'; 'Harsha advanced up to the Narmada River before being forced to retreat'.

region.text: the Narmada, where Pulakeshin II repelled Harsha

ledger.note: Feb 619: Pulakeshin II wins on the Narmada. 'Pulakeshin II repelled an invasion led by Harsha on the banks of Narmada in the winter of 618-619' (Harsha page); 'the Bijapur-Mumbai grant inscription, dated 4 April 619 CE, mentions Pulakeshin's victory over Harsha'.

626: the court moves from Thanesar to Kanyakubja (Kannauj). The pages give no year ('eventually made Kanyakubja ... his capital'); 626 is the midpoint of Harsha's reign, a placeholder. The Kannauj page, opened again, gives no year either ('who made it his capital', r. 606 to 647).

637: Gauda is divided. 'Following his death, Shashanka was succeeded by his son, Manava, who ruled the kingdom for eight months'; 'Gauda was soon divided amongst Harshavardhana and Bhaskarvarmana of Kamarupa'. Shashanka's rule ends 'approximately' 636; the page does not say which share was Harsha's, so Cliopatria's Bengal cells are kept as the reading, minus the Khadga outline (khadga-dynasty holds Vanga and Samatata from 625: the Khadga page 'ruled the areas of Vanga and Samatata ... from 625 CE to 716 CE'; repair of the review finding: two dossiers drew the same 90,000 km2) and minus Karnasuvarna, which kamarupa-kingdom gains in 637. What is left is West Bengal outside Karnasuvarna and northern Bangladesh.

region.text: Harsha's share of Bengal: Gauda 'divided amongst Harshavardhana and Bhaskarvarmana' (Karnasuvarna went to Bhaskarvarman), without the Khadga outline of Vanga and Samatata

ledger.note: c. 640: Valabhi (the Maitrakas) under Harsha. Pushyabhuti page: 'Overlordship was accepted by the king of Vallabhi (west)', undated; 640 is the year the maitraka-dynasty dossier reads from the Maitraka page ('mid-seventh century'), not a page opened here.
647: Valabhi and Kamarupa are free again. The Harsha page gives the death in 647; the end of the overlordship follows from it but is not stated.
647: Bhaskaravarman's alliance ends with Harsha's death; Kamarupa's reign ran to c. 650 and 'the kingdom passed into the hands of Salasthambha (r. 655-670)'.

647: the Later Guptas are independent again. Later Gupta page: 'Madhavagupta, redeclared the independence of the Later Guptas after Harsa's death'; no year is given there, and Harsha died in 647 (Harsha page), the earliest year the page implies (confidence 1).

647: Harsha dies without an heir and the empire ends. 'Died: 647'; 'He died without an heir, leading to the end of the Pushyabhuti dynasty' (Pushyabhuti page); the new king Aluonashun (Arunasva) attacked Wang Xuance's party in 648.

region.text: Harsha's realm at his death: 'much of northern and northwestern India', south to the Narmada, east to Kamarupa, without the Later Gupta vassal Magadha

wars.name: Harsha's campaign against Shashanka of Gauda
wars.outcome: Inconclusive: Harsha 'vowed to destroy the Gauda king', allied with Bhaskar Varman and 'forced Shashanka to retreat', but the Harsha page says the campaign 'remained inconclusive'. Gauda was divided between Harsha and Bhaskarvarman after Shashanka's death (636/637).
wars.note: No fighting year is given on the pages opened (Harsha, Pushyabhuti, Gauda, Kamarupa); the span is the accession to Shashanka's death and no contest zone is drawn.

wars.name: Harsha-Pulakeshin II war on the Narmada
wars.outcome: Pulakeshin II repelled Harsha; the Narmada became the frontier between the Chalukya and Harsha's empires.
wars.note: Bapat and Sohoni date the battle to winter 618-619; K. V. Ramesh and Nilakanta Sastri to c. 612 or before; the Kandalgaon inscription's c. 615 is called spurious.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the pages give regions (north and north-west India, the Narmada in the south, Kamarupa in the east), never a surveyed line. The Narmada frontier after 619 is the best-defined, as a river line between two empires.

notes:
Repair of 2026-10-19 (review finding list sa-03-b-fixed): (1) 606-611 keyframe is now Haryana plus the Kannauj circle, the same land as /ledger/1; the 612 gain counterpart is 'nobody'; /ledger/1 and the other 606 events carry month 4 and follow the found event. (2) The strip south of the Narmada is removed from every correction (Cliopatria error: Pulakeshin II page 'Harsha advanced up to the Narmada River before being forced to retreat'; no page gives Harsha land south of it) and the 619 loss event is deleted, so chalukya-dynasty owes no matching gain. (3) The Khadga outline (Vanga and Samatata, 292 cells) is taken out of the 637 gain and of the 637-646 keyframes; Karnasuvarna (28 cells, kamarupa-kingdom 637) too; the 644 verdict is adjust and the 633-643 shape is split at 637. (4) Magadha is the Later Gupta vassal (Later Gupta page): vassal_start 606 and vassal_end 647 added, Magadha taken out of the direct shapes. (5) Wang Xuance's 648-649 expedition removed from the wars (after the state's end): it belongs to tang-dynasty (ea-04) and arunasva-kannauj, from the Harsha page: 'In 648, Tang Chinese emperor Tang Taizong sent Wang Xuance to India'; he 'fled to Tibet and organized a counterattack with Nepalese and Tibetan forces'; 2,000 prisoners taken in the attack on Magadha; 'The war happened in 649'.
Disagreement with the reviewer: none on substance; I chose removal rather than a mirror gain for the Narmada strip and month 4 (the coronation month) as a placeholder, because the pages give no month for Kannauj or Magadha.
Maukhari land: the maukhari-dynasty dissolve of 606 hands Harsha the Maukhari 602 shape minus Bengal, Bangladesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh, but the pages date only the Kannauj capital loosely ('eventually'); this dossier draws the Kannauj circle in 606 and the rest by 612. The maukhari-dynasty author should shrink the 606 dissolve region to the Kannauj circle and send the rest to 'nobody' until 612 (or widen this dossier's 606 gain instead): either way the two ledgers then agree.
Area: Pushyabhuti infobox 1,000,000 km2 (648 est.); Cliopatria 0.965 M km2 for 633-646; after the corrections about 0.82 M km2 direct (0.86 M with Magadha), ratio 0.82, within a factor of two.
Thin pages: the Harsha, Kannauj, Maukhari and Later Gupta pages give no year for the Kannauj take-over, the Magadha vassalage, Valabhi, Sindh, Kashmir, Nepal or Kamarupa; Pushyabhuti dynasty adds the area (1,000,000 km2 for 648), the 'overlordship' of Valabhi and Kamarupa and C. V. Vaidya's 'nominal suzerainty' of western Punjab and Kashmir (not drawn: nominal, and the kashmir dossier does not treat it as a vassalage).
Cliopatria rows to correct: (1) 612-636 draws Bengal (West Bengal and Bangladesh, 577 cells) as Harsha's although it was Shashanka's Gauda; (2) 612-632 keeps the strip south of the Narmada (377 cells) that no page gives Harsha; (3) 612-646 draws Magadha (162 cells), the Later Gupta vassal, and the Khadga cells (292) of Vanga and Samatata as Harsha's direct land; (4) the 647-655 shape (Bengal, 161,252 km2) outlives Harsha by eight years and is not his land. Cliopatria's Gauda row (602-611) and Khadga row (656-704) draw the same 90,000 km2 of Bengal; the gap 612-655 was filled by Harsha's shape, a Cliopatria artefact.
Disagreements between pages: Pushyabhuti page says Bhaskaravarman accepted Harsha's overlordship, the Kamarupa page speaks of an alliance; the vassal_start for Kamarupa is confidence 1 and the tint is optional. The capital move (626) and the Valabhi vassalage (640) are placeholders (confidence 1).
Still open: the year Harsha took Kannauj and Magadha, the Kalinga/Odisha holdings (R. C. Majumdar's core 'Saurashtra, Kannauj, and Orissa' is on the Pushyabhuti page but undated), Sindh and Nepal (not on the pages), what Arunasva held in 647-649 (needs a dossier: arunasva-kannauj, suggested for the sa-03 additions batch), and the 'Later Gupta' and 'Maukhari' claims to Harsha's land. No gazetteer names are missing: Bengal, Magadha, Haryana, Kannauj, the Narmada river and the Cliopatria shapes all resolve.
